title: Trump Is Linking Economic Investment With Military Alliances: Political Analyst
gist: In a CNBC International interview summarized by CNAS, USC/CNAS analyst Derek Grossman argues Trump is chiefly interested in monetizing US alliances, and that as Washington scales back joint military drills with South Korea, any resulting troop pullback would be very hard to reverse and would raise doubts about US commitment to Asia.

insights.claim: Analyst Derek Grossman argues Trump is most interested in making money off US alliances, framing security ties in transactional economic terms.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A monetized-alliance doctrine implies allies face pay-or-lose-protection pressure—reshaping defense-spending and burden-sharing bets across Asia and Europe.
insights.locator: Derek Grossman from the University of Southern California

insights.claim: The US announced it will scale back from joint military drills with South Korea.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Reduced US-ROK exercises are a concrete signal of retrenchment on the Korean Peninsula—watch for knock-on effects to regional deterrence and defense equities.
insights.quote: the U.S. announces it will scale back from joint military drills with South Korea
insights.locator: as the U.S. announces it will scale back

insights.claim: Grossman warns that once a US pullback from South Korea happens it would be very difficult to redeploy troops to Asia, raising questions about US commitment to the region.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Irreversibility of a drawdown means a one-way credibility loss for US Asia commitments—an escalation-risk factor for Taiwan and broader Indo-Pacific stability.
insights.quote: once this pullback from the U.S. happens, it will be very difficult to redeploy troops to Asia
